claim: Comparison of adipocyte mRNA isolated from mice fed (16 wk) a chow diet (CD) or a high fat diet (HFD) demonstrated differential expression of 4941 genes (q<0.05; absolute log2-fold change >0.75).
source: Comparison of adipocyte mRNA isolated from mice fed (16 wk) a chow diet (CD) or a high fat diet (HFD) demonstrated differential expression of 4941 genes (q<0.05; absolute log2-fold change >0.75) and differential inclusion/exclusion of 1631 exons (FDR<0.05; absolute change in exon inclusion (absolute ∆Inc level) >0.1) (corresponding to 1249 genes) in the transcriptome (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data analysis with specific statistical thresholds (q<0.05, log2-fold change >0.75) and referenced to Figure 1A.

claim: Comparison of adipocyte mRNA isolated from mice fed (16 wk) a chow diet (CD) or a high fat diet (HFD) demonstrated differential inclusion/exclusion of 1631 exons (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) corresponding to 1249 genes in the transcriptome.
source: Comparison of adipocyte mRNA isolated from mice fed (16 wk) a chow diet (CD) or a high fat diet (HFD) demonstrated differential expression of 4941 genes (q<0.05; absolute log2-fold change >0.75) and differential inclusion/exclusion of 1631 exons (FDR<0.05; absolute change in exon inclusion (absolute ∆Inc level) >0.1) (corresponding to 1249 genes) in the transcriptome (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: Supported by RNA sequencing data analysis with specific statistical thresholds (FDR<0.05, absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) and referenced to Figure 1A and supplementary figures.

claim: Only 6.4% of the differentially expressed genes were alternatively spliced.
source: Only 6.4% of the differentially expressed genes were alternatively spliced, but 25% of the alternatively spliced genes were differentially expressed (Figure 1B).
evidence: Calculated from the overlap between differentially expressed genes and alternatively spliced genes, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 25% of the alternatively spliced genes were differentially expressed.
source: Only 6.4% of the differentially expressed genes were alternatively spliced, but 25% of the alternatively spliced genes were differentially expressed (Figure 1B).
evidence: Calculated from the overlap between differentially expressed genes and alternatively spliced genes, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The genomic response to the consumption of a HFD causes quantitative changes in both gene expression and alternative pre-mRNA splicing in adipocytes.
source: These data indicate that the genomic response to the consumption of a HFD causes quantitative changes in both gene expression and alternative pre-mRNA splicing in adipocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the RNA-seq data showing both differential gene expression and alternative splicing in response to HFD.

claim: The most common form of HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing was exon skipping (1052 exons).
source: The most common form of HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing was exon skipping (1052 exons), but we also detected 144 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 160 retained introns, 123 alternative 5' splice sites, and 152 alternative 3' splice sites (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis categorizing types of alternative splicing events, referenced to Figure 1C,D.

claim: HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing included 144 mutually exclusive exon inclusions.
source: The most common form of HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing was exon skipping (1052 exons), but we also detected 144 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 160 retained introns, 123 alternative 5' splice sites, and 152 alternative 3' splice sites (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis categorizing types of alternative splicing events, referenced to Figure 1C,D.

claim: HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing included 160 retained introns.
source: The most common form of HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing was exon skipping (1052 exons), but we also detected 144 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 160 retained introns, 123 alternative 5' splice sites, and 152 alternative 3' splice sites (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis categorizing types of alternative splicing events, referenced to Figure 1C,D.

claim: HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing included 123 alternative 5' splice sites.
source: The most common form of HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing was exon skipping (1052 exons), but we also detected 144 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 160 retained introns, 123 alternative 5' splice sites, and 152 alternative 3' splice sites (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis categorizing types of alternative splicing events, referenced to Figure 1C,D.

claim: HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing included 152 alternative 3' splice sites.
source: The most common form of HFD-induced alternative pre-mRNA splicing was exon skipping (1052 exons), but we also detected 144 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 160 retained introns, 123 alternative 5' splice sites, and 152 alternative 3' splice sites (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis categorizing types of alternative splicing events, referenced to Figure 1C,D.

claim: Few HFD-regulated alternative pre-mRNA splicing events were detected in liver, including 2 skipped exons, 0 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 13 retained introns, 1 alternative 5' splice site, and 1 alternative 3' splice site (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1).
source: In contrast to the extensive changes in alternative pre-mRNA splicing in adipocytes caused by diet-induced obesity (Figure 1A–C) few HFD-regulated alternative pre-mRNA splicing events were detected in liver, although we did find 2 skipped exons, 0 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 13 retained introns, 1 alternative 5' splice site, and 1 alternative 3' splice site (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis of liver tissue comparing CD and HFD conditions.

claim: Widespread changes in pre-mRNA splicing are not a general response to diet-induced obesity, but a selective response of white adipocytes to the consumption of a HFD.
source: This comparative analysis of gene expression indicates that widespread changes in pre-mRNA splicing are not a general response to diet-induced obesity, but a selective response of white adipocytes to the consumption of a HFD.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of extensive splicing changes in adipocytes versus minimal changes in liver in response to HFD.

claim: Increased inclusion of Fyn exon 7b, compared with exon 7a, in response to the consumption of an HFD is anticipated to increase FYN tyrosine kinase activity.
source: Increased inclusion of Fyn exon 7b, compared with exon 7a, in response to the consumption of an HFD (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) is anticipated to increase FYN tyrosine kinase activity (Brignatz et al., 2009) leading to suppression of fatty acid oxidation and promotion of insulin resistance (Bastie et al., 2007).
evidence: Based on RNA-seq data showing differential exon inclusion and cited literature (Brignatz et al., 2009) on FYN kinase activity.

claim: Increased FYN tyrosine kinase activity leads to suppression of fatty acid oxidation and promotion of insulin resistance.
source: Increased inclusion of Fyn exon 7b, compared with exon 7a, in response to the consumption of an HFD (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) is anticipated to increase FYN tyrosine kinase activity (Brignatz et al., 2009) leading to suppression of fatty acid oxidation and promotion of insulin resistance (Bastie et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bastie et al., 2007.

claim: Alternative pre-mRNA splicing may contribute to the adipocyte response to obesity.
source: Together, these data indicate that alternative pre-mRNA splicing may contribute to the adipocyte response to obesity.
evidence: Inferred from the observed changes in alternative splicing in response to HFD and the functional implications of specific splicing events.

claim: Bioinformatics analysis identified potential binding sites (YCAY) for NOVA alternative pre-mRNA splicing factors.
source: To gain insight into the mechanism of HFD-induced pre-mRNA splicing, we examined exons (plus 500 bp of flanking intron sequence) to identify potential motifs that were significantly enriched for alternatively spliced exons. This analysis led to the identification of potential binding sites (YCAY) for NOVA alternative pre-mRNA splicing factors (Darnell, 2013).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatics analysis of exon sequences and cited literature (Darnell, 2013) on NOVA binding sites.

claim: There is significant (p<2.2 × 10−16) enrichment of UV-mediated cross-linking and immunoprecipitation sequencing (CLIP-seq) tags for NOVA proteins within the HFD-induced group of alternatively spliced exons in adipocytes.
source: Indeed, we found significant (p<2.2 × 10−16) enrichment of UV-mediated cross-linking and immunoprecipitation sequencing (CLIP-seq) tags for NOVA proteins identified in brain tissue (Licatalosi et al., 2008) within the HFD-induced group of alternatively spliced exons in adipocytes (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of NOVA CLIP-seq data overlap with HFD-induced alternatively spliced exons, referenced to Figure 1E and Licatalosi et al., 2008.

claim: The NOVA CLIP-seq tags intersected with 56% of the HFD-induced alternatively spliced exons (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1).
source: The NOVA CLIP-seq tags intersected with 56% of the HFD-induced alternatively spliced exons (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1E) and were associated with both HFD-induced exon inclusion (53% intersection) and HFD-induced exon exclusion (62% intersection), consistent with the known role of NOVA proteins to cause context-dependent exon inclusion/exclusion (Ule et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatics analysis of NOVA CLIP-seq tag overlap with alternatively spliced exons, referenced to Figure 1E and Ule et al., 2006.

claim: NOVA CLIP-seq tags were associated with both HFD-induced exon inclusion (53% intersection) and HFD-induced exon exclusion (62% intersection).
source: The NOVA CLIP-seq tags intersected with 56% of the HFD-induced alternatively spliced exons (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1E) and were associated with both HFD-induced exon inclusion (53% intersection) and HFD-induced exon exclusion (62% intersection), consistent with the known role of NOVA proteins to cause context-dependent exon inclusion/exclusion (Ule et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatics analysis of NOVA CLIP-seq tag overlap with alternatively spliced exons, referenced to Figure 1E and Ule et al., 2006.

claim: NOVA proteins cause context-dependent exon inclusion/exclusion.
source: The NOVA CLIP-seq tags intersected with 56% of the HFD-induced alternatively spliced exons (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) (Figure 1E) and were associated with both HFD-induced exon inclusion (53% intersection) and HFD-induced exon exclusion (62% intersection), consistent with the known role of NOVA proteins to cause context-dependent exon inclusion/exclusion (Ule et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ule et al., 2006.

claim: Bioinformatics analysis implicates a role for NOVA proteins in a sub-set of HFD-induced alternative splicing events.
source: This analysis implicates a role for NOVA proteins in a sub-set of HFD-induced alternative splicing events.
evidence: Inferred from the enrichment of NOVA binding sites and CLIP-seq tags in HFD-induced alternatively spliced exons.

claim: NOVA proteins are expressed in several tissues, including neurons, vascular endothelial cells, and pancreatic β cells.
source: NOVA proteins are expressed in several tissues, including neurons (Darnell, 2013), vascular endothelial cells (Giampietro et al., 2015), and pancreatic β cells (Villate et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Darnell, 2013; Giampietro et al., 2015; and Villate et al., 2014.

claim: NOVA proteins were not detected in liver.
source: Indeed, NOVA proteins were not detected in liver, but both NOVA1 and NOVA2 proteins were found in white adipocytes (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Both NOVA1 and NOVA2 proteins were found in white adipocytes.
source: Indeed, NOVA proteins were not detected in liver, but both NOVA1 and NOVA2 proteins were found in white adipocytes (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Nova gene expression in white adipocytes was partially reduced in obese humans and mice.
source: Interestingly, Nova gene expression in white adipocytes was partially reduced in obese humans and mice (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 5) and in mice fed a HFD (Figure 1H).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1G, Figure 1H, and Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Nova gene expression in white adipocytes was partially reduced in mice fed a HFD.
source: Interestingly, Nova gene expression in white adipocytes was partially reduced in obese humans and mice (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 5) and in mice fed a HFD (Figure 1H).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The decrease in NOVA expression may be relevant to obesity-regulated changes in alternative pre-mRNA splicing in adipocytes.
source: This decrease in NOVA expression may be relevant to obesity-regulated changes in alternative pre-mRNA splicing in adipocytes.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the observed correlation between decreased NOVA expression and alternative splicing changes in obesity.

claim: The absence of NOVA expression in liver may contribute to the minimal effect of HFD consumption on alternative splicing of pre-mRNA in the liver.
source: Moreover, the absence of NOVA expression in liver (Figure 1F) may contribute to the minimal effect of HFD consumption on alternative splicing of pre-mRNA in the liver.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between lack of NOVA expression in liver and minimal splicing changes in liver in response to HFD.

claim: Reduced expression of Nova1 or Nova2 in mice causes developmental defects and neonatal lethality.
source: Reduced expression of Nova1 or Nova2 in mice causes developmental defects and neonatal lethality (Jensen et al., 2000; Ruggiu et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jensen et al., 2000 and Ruggiu et al., 2009.

claim: Compound NOVA1/2 deficiency caused only a small change in gene expression (55 genes; q<0.05; absolute log2-fold change >0.75).
source: Compound NOVA1/2 deficiency caused only a small change in gene expression (55 genes; q<0.05; absolute log2-fold change >0.75), but NOVA1/2 deficiency caused a large change in differential exon inclusion/exclusion (1169 exons; FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) in the adipocyte transcriptome (Figure 2A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of FWT and F∆N1,2 mice, referenced to Figure 2A.

claim: NOVA1/2 deficiency caused a large change in differential exon inclusion/exclusion (1169 exons; FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) in the adipocyte transcriptome.
source: Compound NOVA1/2 deficiency caused only a small change in gene expression (55 genes; q<0.05; absolute log2-fold change >0.75), but NOVA1/2 deficiency caused a large change in differential exon inclusion/exclusion (1169 exons; FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) in the adipocyte transcriptome (Figure 2A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of FWT and F∆N1,2 mice, referenced to Figure 2A.

claim: NOVA deficiency primarily changes pre-mRNA splicing.
source: These data indicate that NOVA deficiency primarily changes pre-mRNA splicing.
evidence: Inferred from the large number of splicing changes (1169 exons) versus small number of gene expression changes (55 genes) in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: The most common form of alternative pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA deficiency was exon skipping (768 exons).
source: The most common form of alternative pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA deficiency was exon skipping (768 exons), but we also detected 128 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 99 intron retentions, 64 alternative 5' splice sites, and 110 alternative 3' splice sites (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of NOVA-deficient mice, referenced to Figure 2D,E.

claim: NOVA deficiency caused 128 mutually exclusive exon inclusions.
source: The most common form of alternative pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA deficiency was exon skipping (768 exons), but we also detected 128 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 99 intron retentions, 64 alternative 5' splice sites, and 110 alternative 3' splice sites (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of NOVA-deficient mice, referenced to Figure 2D,E.

claim: NOVA deficiency caused 99 intron retentions.
source: The most common form of alternative pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA deficiency was exon skipping (768 exons), but we also detected 128 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 99 intron retentions, 64 alternative 5' splice sites, and 110 alternative 3' splice sites (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of NOVA-deficient mice, referenced to Figure 2D,E.

claim: NOVA deficiency caused 64 alternative 5' splice sites.
source: The most common form of alternative pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA deficiency was exon skipping (768 exons), but we also detected 128 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 99 intron retentions, 64 alternative 5' splice sites, and 110 alternative 3' splice sites (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of NOVA-deficient mice, referenced to Figure 2D,E.

claim: NOVA deficiency caused 110 alternative 3' splice sites.
source: The most common form of alternative pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA deficiency was exon skipping (768 exons), but we also detected 128 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 99 intron retentions, 64 alternative 5' splice sites, and 110 alternative 3' splice sites (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of NOVA-deficient mice, referenced to Figure 2D,E.

claim: Single gene ablations of Nova1 or Nova2 identified fewer changes in alternative pre-mRNA splicing, including 10 & 7 skipped exons, 1 & 4 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 12 & 16 intron retentions, 1 & 0 alternative 5' splice sites, and 2 & 4 alternative 3' splice sites, respectively (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1).
source: Analysis of white adipocytes with single gene ablations of Nova1 or Nova2 identified fewer changes in alternative pre-mRNA splicing, including 10 & 7 skipped exons, 1 & 4 mutually exclusive exon inclusions, 12 & 16 intron retentions, 1 & 0 alternative 5' splice sites, and 2 & 4 alternative 3' splice sites, respectively (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of single Nova1 or Nova2 knockout mice.

claim: NOVA1 and NOVA2 can cause isoform-specific changes in adipocyte pre-mRNA alternative splicing.
source: These data indicate that NOVA1 and NOVA2 can cause isoform-specific changes in adipocyte pre-mRNA alternative splicing.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that single gene ablations cause some splicing changes.

claim: NOVA proteins exhibit some functional redundancy in adipocytes.
source: However, the effect of compound NOVA1 plus NOVA2 deficiency to cause widespread changes in alternative pre-mRNA splicing (Figure 2) indicates that these NOVA proteins exhibit some functional redundancy in adipocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of single versus double knockout effects on alternative splicing.

claim: 323 genes are co-regulated by alternative pre-mRNA splicing following HFD consumption and NOVA deficiency.
source: Comparison of white adipocyte genes with differential alternative splicing (FDR<0.05; absolute ∆Inc level >0.1) caused by the consumption of a HFD (Figure 1A) or NOVA1/2 deficiency (Figure 2B) demonstrated 323 co-regulated genes (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The 323 co-regulated genes represent 26% of the 1249 HFD-regulated genes and 34% of the 950 NOVA-regulated genes.
source: These co-regulated genes represent 26% of the 1249 HFD-regulated genes and 34% of the 950 NOVA-regulated genes.
evidence: Calculated from the overlap between HFD-regulated and NOVA-regulated alternatively spliced genes.

claim: Adipocytes and hepatocytes express different alternatively spliced JNK isoforms.
source: This analysis demonstrated that adipocytes and hepatocytes express different alternatively spliced JNK isoforms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by Taqman assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Tissue-specific differences in Mapk8/9 pre-mRNA splicing may be influenced by the selective expression of NOVA proteins in adipocytes, but not hepatocytes.
source: These tissue-specific differences in Mapk8/9 pre-mRNA splicing may be influenced by the selective expression of NOVA proteins in adipocytes, but not hepatocytes (Figures 1F and 3A), although NOVA-independent mechanisms likely also contribute to the observed cell type-specific pattern of JNK isoform expression.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the correlation between NOVA expression patterns and JNK isoform expression patterns.

claim: Hepatic expression of NOVA2 caused a decrease in the Mapk8α/β ratio.
source: We found that hepatic expression of NOVA2 caused a decrease in the Mapk8α/β ratio and an increase in the Mapk9α/β ratio, indicating that NOVA can promote the expression of the Mapk8β and Mapk9α alternatively spliced isoforms (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Hepatic expression of NOVA2 caused an increase in the Mapk9α/β ratio.
source: We found that hepatic expression of NOVA2 caused a decrease in the Mapk8α/β ratio and an increase in the Mapk9α/β ratio, indicating that NOVA can promote the expression of the Mapk8β and Mapk9α alternatively spliced isoforms (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NOVA can promote the expression of the Mapk8β and Mapk9α alternatively spliced isoforms.
source: We found that hepatic expression of NOVA2 caused a decrease in the Mapk8α/β ratio and an increase in the Mapk9α/β ratio, indicating that NOVA can promote the expression of the Mapk8β and Mapk9α alternatively spliced isoforms (Figure 3B).
evidence: Inferred from the observed changes in Mapk8 and Mapk9 isoform ratios upon NOVA2 expression.

claim: Adipocyte-specific deficiency of NOVA1 plus NOVA2 caused an increase in the Mapk8α/β ratio.
source: In contrast, adipocyte-specific deficiency of NOVA1 plus NOVA2 caused an increase in the Mapk8α/β ratio and a decrease in the Mapk9α/β ratio, indicating that NOVA-deficiency promotes the expression of the Mapk8α and Mapk9β alternatively spliced isoforms (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Adipocyte-specific deficiency of NOVA1 plus NOVA2 caused a decrease in the Mapk9α/β ratio.
source: In contrast, adipocyte-specific deficiency of NOVA1 plus NOVA2 caused an increase in the Mapk8α/β ratio and a decrease in the Mapk9α/β ratio, indicating that NOVA-deficiency promotes the expression of the Mapk8α and Mapk9β alternatively spliced isoforms (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: NOVA-deficiency promotes the expression of the Mapk8α and Mapk9β alternatively spliced isoforms.
source: In contrast, adipocyte-specific deficiency of NOVA1 plus NOVA2 caused an increase in the Mapk8α/β ratio and a decrease in the Mapk9α/β ratio, indicating that NOVA-deficiency promotes the expression of the Mapk8α and Mapk9β alternatively spliced isoforms (Figure 3C).
evidence: Inferred from the observed changes in Mapk8 and Mapk9 isoform ratios in NOVA-deficient adipocytes.

claim: HFD consumption causes significant changes in the mutually exclusive inclusion of Mapk8 exons 7a and 7b (FDR=0.0066).
source: These observations are consistent with the finding that HFD consumption causes both decreased NOVA expression (Figure 1H) and significant changes in the mutually exclusive inclusion of Mapk8 exons 7a and 7b (FDR=0.0066).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis showing differential splicing of Mapk8 exons in response to HFD.

claim: NOVA proteins can promote the expression of the Mapk8β and Mapk9α isoforms.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that NOVA proteins can promote the expression of the Mapk8β and Mapk9α isoforms.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results of NOVA overexpression and deficiency experiments.

claim: The sequence differences between the α and β isoforms of JNK1 and JNK2 are located in the substrate binding site.
source: The sequence differences between the α and β isoforms of JNK1 and JNK2 are located in the substrate binding site (Figure 3D) and influence the interaction of JNK with protein substrates (Davis, 2000).
evidence: Supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 3D and citation to Davis, 2000.

claim: The sequence differences between the α and β isoforms of JNK1 and JNK2 influence the interaction of JNK with protein substrates.
source: The sequence differences between the α and β isoforms of JNK1 and JNK2 are located in the substrate binding site (Figure 3D) and influence the interaction of JNK with protein substrates (Davis, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Davis, 2000.

claim: JNK1α and JNK2β represent low activity forms of JNK protein kinases.
source: Studies using the substrate cJun demonstrate low activity (JNK1α and JNK2β) and high activity (JNK1β and JNK2α) groups of JNK protein kinases in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and in vivo (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and in vivo data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: JNK1β and JNK2α represent high activity forms of JNK protein kinases.
source: Studies using the substrate cJun demonstrate low activity (JNK1α and JNK2β) and high activity (JNK1β and JNK2α) groups of JNK protein kinases in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and in vivo (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and in vivo data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: NOVA-deficiency can be predicted to cause expression of the low activity forms JNK1α and JNK2β in adipocytes.
source: Since NOVA can promote the expression of Mapk8β and Mapk9α mRNA that encode the high activity forms of JNK1 and JNK2, NOVA-deficiency can be predicted to cause expression of the low activity forms JNK1α and JNK2β in adipocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the observed effects of NOVA on Mapk8/9 splicing and the known activity differences between JNK isoforms.

claim: No differences in JNK expression or stress-induced activating phosphorylation (pThr180-Pro-pTyr182) of JNK between FWT and F∆N1,2 adipocytes were detected by immunoblot analysis.
source: No differences in JNK expression or stress-induced activating phosphorylation (pThr180-Pro-pTyr182) of JNK between FWT and F∆N1,2 adipocytes were detected by immunoblot analysis (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Stress-induced phosphorylation of the JNK substrate pSer63 cJun was markedly suppressed in F∆N1,2 adipocytes compared with FWT adipocytes.
source: However, stress-induced phosphorylation of the JNK substrate pSer63 cJun was markedly suppressed in F∆N1,2 adipocytes compared with FWT adipocytes (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: NOVA proteins can regulate signaling mechanisms in adipocytes.
source: Together, these data confirm that NOVA proteins can regulate signaling mechanisms in adipocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the observed effects of NOVA deficiency on JNK signaling.

claim: F∆J1,2 mice with adipocyte-specific JNK-deficiency exhibited increased core body temperature.
source: These mice exhibited increased core body temperature and increased expression of genes that mediate sympathetic activation (Adr3b) and thermogenesis (Ucp1) in adipocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by telemetry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: F∆J1,2 mice with adipocyte-specific JNK-deficiency exhibited increased expression of genes that mediate sympathetic activation (Adr3b) and thermogenesis (Ucp1) in adipocytes.
source: These mice exhibited increased core body temperature and increased expression of genes that mediate sympathetic activation (Adr3b) and thermogenesis (Ucp1) in adipocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: CD-fed FWT and F∆N1,2 mice gained similar body mass.
source: We found that CD-fed FWT and F∆N1,2 mice gained similar body mass, but HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice gained significantly less mass than HFD-fed FWT mice (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by body mass measurements shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice gained significantly less mass than HFD-fed FWT mice.
source: We found that CD-fed FWT and F∆N1,2 mice gained similar body mass, but HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice gained significantly less mass than HFD-fed FWT mice (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by body mass measurements shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The decreased body mass in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice was caused by reduced fat mass.
source: Proton magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated that the decreased body mass was caused by reduced fat mass (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by proton magnetic resonance imaging data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice showed a reduction in mass of the liver and adipose tissue compared with HFD-fed FWT mice.
source: Analysis of organs at necropsy demonstrated a reduction in mass of the liver and adipose tissue in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice compared with HFD-fed FWT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) and analysis of tissue sections demonstrated reduced adipocyte hypertrophy, reduced hepatic steatosis, and reduced hypertrophy of pancreatic islets in the NOVA-deficient mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by organ mass measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NOVA-deficient mice showed reduced adipocyte hypertrophy, reduced hepatic steatosis, and reduced hypertrophy of pancreatic islets.
source: Analysis of organs at necropsy demonstrated a reduction in mass of the liver and adipose tissue in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice compared with HFD-fed FWT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) and analysis of tissue sections demonstrated reduced adipocyte hypertrophy, reduced hepatic steatosis, and reduced hypertrophy of pancreatic islets in the NOVA-deficient mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Hyperinsulinemia and hyperleptinemia were reduced in F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice.
source: Indeed, hyperinsulinemia and hyperleptinemia were reduced in F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by blood insulin and leptin measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claim: HFD-fed FWT mice were found to be more glucose intolerant than F∆N1,2 mice.
source: Moreover, HFD-fed FWT mice were found to be more glucose intolerant than F∆N1,2 mice (Figure 4D) and the HFD-induced hyperglycemia observed in FWT mice was suppressed in F∆N1,2 mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The HFD-induced hyperglycemia observed in FWT mice was suppressed in F∆N1,2 mice.
source: Moreover, HFD-fed FWT mice were found to be more glucose intolerant than F∆N1,2 mice (Figure 4D) and the HFD-induced hyperglycemia observed in FWT mice was suppressed in F∆N1,2 mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by blood glucose measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Food/water consumption and physical activity of FWT and F∆N1,2 mice were similar.
source: Metabolic cage analysis demonstrated that food/water consumption and physical activity of FWT and F∆N1,2 mice were similar (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), but F∆N1,2 mice exhibited greatly increased energy expenditure compared with FWT mice (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by metabolic cage data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: F∆N1,2 mice exhibited greatly increased energy expenditure compared with FWT mice.
source: Metabolic cage analysis demonstrated that food/water consumption and physical activity of FWT and F∆N1,2 mice were similar (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), but F∆N1,2 mice exhibited greatly increased energy expenditure compared with FWT mice (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by metabolic cage data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: The increase in energy expenditure may account for the suppression of HFD-induced obesity caused by NOVA deficiency in adipocytes.
source: This increase in energy expenditure may account for the suppression of HFD-induced obesity caused by NOVA deficiency in adipocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between increased energy expenditure and reduced obesity in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: NOVA proteins in adipocytes suppress energy expenditure and promote obesity-associated metabolic syndrome.
source: These data demonstrate that NOVA proteins in adipocytes suppress energy expenditure and promote obesity-associated metabolic syndrome.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotypic analysis of NOVA-deficient mice showing increased energy expenditure and improved metabolic parameters.

claim: The core body temperature of F∆N1,2 mice was significantly higher than FWT mice during the course of the cold challenge study.
source: This analysis demonstrated that the core body temperature of F∆N1,2 mice was significantly higher than FWT mice during the course of this study (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by telemetry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: F∆N1,2 mice showed increased expression of genes in sub-cutaneous adipocytes that are associated with a 'browning' (beige/brite) phenotype (Cidea, Dio2, Ppargc1a, Ppargc1b, and Ucp1) compared with FWT mice.
source: This was associated with increased expression of genes in sub-cutaneous adipocytes of F∆N1,2 mice that are associated with a 'browning' (beige/brite) phenotype (Cidea, Dio2, Ppargc1a, Ppargc1b, and Ucp1) compared with FWT mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: NOVA proteins in adipocytes can suppress adipose tissue thermogenesis.
source: Together, these data indicate that NOVA proteins in adipocytes can suppress adipose tissue thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the increased thermogenesis observed in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: F∆N1,2 mice and FWT mice gained equal body mass at thermoneutrality (30°C).
source: We found that F∆N1,2 mice and FWT mice gained equal body mass at thermoneutrality (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by body mass measurements at 30°C shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The increased glucose tolerance of F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was not observed at 30°C.
source: Moreover, the increased glucose tolerance of F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was not observed at 30°C (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by glucose tolerance test data at 30°C shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The improved glycemic regulation exhibited by F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was caused by increased thermogenesis.
source: These data indicate that the improved glycemic regulation exhibited by F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was caused by increased thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the loss of improved glycemia at thermoneutrality where thermogenesis is not required.

claim: The reduced adipocyte hypertrophy observed in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was not observed at 30°C.
source: Consistent with this conclusion, we found that the reduced adipocyte hypertrophy observed in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was not observed at 30°C (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The increased expression of thermogenesis-related genes (Adrb3, Cidea, Dio2, Ppargc1a/b Prdm16, and Ucp1) by adipocytes in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was not found at 30°C.
source: Similarly, the increased expression of thermogenesis-related genes (Adrb3, Cidea, Dio2, Ppargc1a/b Prdm16, and Ucp1) by adipocytes in HFD-fed F∆N1,2 mice compared with FWT mice at 21°C was not found at 30°C (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Adipose tissue thermogenesis contributes to the improved glycemia of mice with NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that adipose tissue thermogenesis contributes to the improved glycemia of mice with NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the loss of improved glycemia at thermoneutrality where thermogenesis is not required.

claim: The browning of white adipose tissue is associated with the appearance of beige/brite adipocytes, increased energy expenditure, and improved obesity-induced metabolic syndrome.
source: The browning of white adipose tissue is associated with the appearance of beige/brite adipocytes, increased energy expenditure, and improved obesity-induced metabolic syndrome (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014.

claim: Beige/brite adipocytes in white adipose tissue depots can arise from specialized progenitor cells.
source: It is established that beige/brite adipocytes in white adipose tissue depots can arise from specialized progenitor cells (Wang et al., 2013b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2013b.

claim: Beige/brite adipocytes may also arise from inactive cells present within white adipose tissue.
source: Beige/brite adipocytes may also arise from inactive cells present within white adipose tissue (Rosenwald et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rosenwald et al., 2013.

claim: The increased adipose tissue browning detected in mice with adipocyte-specific NOVA deficiency does not likely reflect a change in adipocyte differentiation from specialized progenitor cells, but rather a change in mature adipocyte function.
source: The increased adipose tissue browning detected in mice with adipocyte-specific NOVA deficiency was observed using floxed Nova alleles and a Cre driver (Adipoq-Cre) that is expressed in mature adipocytes. It is therefore likely that the increased white adipose tissue browning caused by NOVA deficiency does not reflect a change in adipocyte differentiation from specialized progenitor cells, but rather a change in mature adipocyte function.
evidence: Inferred from the use of Adipoq-Cre which is expressed in mature adipocytes, not progenitor cells.

claim: Housing mice at thermoneutrality prevents the effect of NOVA deficiency to cause 'browning'.
source: However, the observation that housing mice at thermoneutrality prevents the effect of NOVA deficiency to cause 'browning' suggests that NOVA deficiency may act by promoting the activation of inactive beige/brite adipocytes.
evidence: Supported by the data showing loss of browning phenotype at thermoneutrality.

claim: NOVA deficiency may act by promoting the activation of inactive beige/brite adipocytes.
source: However, the observation that housing mice at thermoneutrality prevents the effect of NOVA deficiency to cause 'browning' suggests that NOVA deficiency may act by promoting the activation of inactive beige/brite adipocytes.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the temperature-dependent browning phenotype.

claim: NOVA expression in white adipocytes is reduced in obese humans and mice.
source: Our analysis demonstrates that NOVA expression in white adipocytes is reduced in obese humans and mice (Figure 1).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1G, 1H, and Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Compound NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes caused increased adipose tissue thermogenesis and improved whole body glycemia in HFD-fed mice.
source: Gene knockout studies demonstrate that compound NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes caused increased adipose tissue thermogenesis and improved whole body glycemia in HFD-fed mice (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Partial NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes caused modest changes in adipocyte physiology.
source: However, partial NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes (potentially modeling the changes in NOVA expression caused by feeding a HFD) caused modest changes in adipocyte physiology (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by phenotypic analysis of single Nova knockout mice shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: NOVA proteins in adipocytes function to suppress adipose tissue thermogenesis.
source: Nevertheless, our data establish that NOVA proteins in adipocytes function to suppress adipose tissue thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the increased thermogenesis observed in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: The mechanism by which NOVA proteins suppress thermogenesis appears to be mediated by NOVA-regulated changes in pre-mRNA splicing that promote adipocyte thermogenic gene expression.
source: The mechanism appears to be mediated by NOVA-regulated changes in pre-mRNA splicing that promote adipocyte thermogenic gene expression (Figure 5), but we cannot exclude additional contributions caused by other biochemical actions of NOVA proteins, including alternative mRNA polyadenylation (Licatalosi et al., 2008) and functional regulation of Argonaute/microRNA complexes (Storchel et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5 and cited literature on NOVA functions.

claim: NOVA proteins do function as alternative pre-mRNA splicing factors in adipocytes.
source: However, our analysis demonstrates that NOVA proteins do function as alternative pre-mRNA splicing factors in adipocytes (Figure 2).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis of NOVA-deficient mice shown in Figure 2.

claim: The changes in pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA proteins include both increased and decreased exon inclusion.
source: The changes in pre-mRNA splicing caused by NOVA proteins include both increased and decreased exon inclusion, consistent with the known context-dependent role of NOVA proteins to promote both exon inclusion and exclusion (Ule et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and citation to Ule et al., 2006.

claim: NOVA proteins may act in a combinatorial manner with other splicing factors.
source: First, NOVA proteins may act in a combinatorial manner with other splicing factors (Zhang et al., 2010), but roles for such factors in adipocytes have not been established.
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2010, but noted as not yet established in adipocytes.

claim: NOVA proteins contribute to the alternative splicing of 26% of the genes that are regulated by HFD consumption.
source: Second, our analysis of mice with NOVA-deficiency in adipocytes implicates a role for NOVA proteins in the alternative splicing of 26% of the genes that are regulated by HFD consumption (Figure 2B).
evidence: Calculated from the overlap between HFD-regulated and NOVA-regulated alternatively spliced genes shown in Figure 2B.

claim: NOVA proteins do not contribute to 74% of the genes that exhibit HFD-regulated pre-mRNA splicing.
source: Consequently, NOVA proteins do not contribute to 74% of the genes that exhibit HFD-regulated pre-mRNA splicing and mechanisms that contribute to the regulation of these genes have not been established.
evidence: Calculated from the overlap analysis showing 26% NOVA-dependent and therefore 74% NOVA-independent HFD-regulated splicing.

claim: The regulation of adipose tissue thermogenesis by NOVA proteins may not be entirely dependent upon the classical UCP1 pathway because of the existence of alternative thermogenic mechanisms.
source: The regulation of adipose tissue thermogenesis by NOVA proteins may not be entirely dependent upon the classical UCP1 pathway (Kozak, 2010) because of the existence of alternative thermogenic mechanisms (Kazak et al., 2015).
evidence: Speculative statement supported by citations to Kozak, 2010 and Kazak et al., 2015.

claim: NOVA proteins can suppress adipocyte thermogenesis.
source: Nevertheless, our data demonstrate that NOVA proteins can suppress adipocyte thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the increased thermogenesis observed in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: Reduced NOVA expression in adipocytes causes thermogenesis.
source: Reduced NOVA expression in adipocytes causes thermogenesis (Figure 5) and may potentially be achieved by drugs targeting NOVA-mediated pre-mRNA splicing.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5 showing increased thermogenesis in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: Reduced NOVA expression in adipocytes may potentially be achieved by drugs targeting NOVA-mediated pre-mRNA splicing.
source: Reduced NOVA expression in adipocytes causes thermogenesis (Figure 5) and may potentially be achieved by drugs targeting NOVA-mediated pre-mRNA splicing.
evidence: Speculative statement about potential therapeutic application.

claim: The role of NOVA proteins is most likely mediated by a network response to a pre-mRNA splicing program that collectively regulates adipocyte thermogenesis.
source: This role of NOVA proteins is most likely mediated by a network response to a pre-mRNA splicing program that collectively regulates adipocyte thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the large number of genes affected by NOVA-mediated splicing.

claim: A NOVA-dependent alternative pre-mRNA splicing program in white adipocytes regulates browning of white adipose tissue.
source: In conclusion, we describe a NOVA-dependent alternative pre-mRNA splicing program in white adipocytes that regulates browning of white adipose tissue.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Alternative pre-mRNA splicing is a biological process that may be targeted by drugs designed to increase adipocyte thermogenesis and improve metabolic syndrome caused by obesity.
source: These data identify alternative pre-mRNA splicing as a biological process that may be targeted by drugs designed to increase adipocyte thermogenesis and improve metabolic syndrome caused by obesity.
evidence: Speculative statement about potential therapeutic implications of the findings.

claim: Treatment of primary adipocytes with forskolin increases cAMP concentration and promotes the beige/brite phenotype.
source: Indeed, treatment of primary adipocytes with the drug forskolin increases cAMP concentration and promotes the beige/brite phenotype (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014), and causes increased expression of the Adrb3, Dio2, Fgf21, Ppargc1a, and Ucp1 genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citation to Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014.

claim: Forskolin treatment causes increased expression of the Adrb3, Dio2, Fgf21, Ppargc1a, and Ucp1 genes in primary adipocytes.
source: Indeed, treatment of primary adipocytes with the drug forskolin increases cAMP concentration and promotes the beige/brite phenotype (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014), and causes increased expression of the Adrb3, Dio2, Fgf21, Ppargc1a, and Ucp1 genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Forskolin treatment causes decreased Nova gene expression and promotes expression of the alternatively spliced isoform Mapk9β.
source: This treatment also causes decreased Nova gene expression and promotes expression of the alternatively spliced isoform Mapk9β (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NOVA-deficiency caused increased expression of genes in adipocytes that mediate sympathetic activation (Adrb3) and thermogenesis (Ucp1).
source: This analysis demonstrated that NOVA-deficiency caused increased expression of genes in adipocytes that mediate sympathetic activation (Adrb3) and thermogenesis (Ucp1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data from primary adipocytes shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 3T3L1 adipocytes express NOVA1, but NOVA2 was not detected.
source: These cells express NOVA1, but NOVA2 was not detected.
evidence: Implicit from the experimental design using 3T3L1 cells for Nova1 knockdown studies.

claim: Nova1 knock-down using shRNA was associated with increased expression of the beige/brite phenotype genes Prdm16 and Ucp1 in 3T3L1 adipocytes.
source: Nova1 knock-down using shRNA was associated with increased expression of the beige/brite phenotype genes Prdm16 and Ucp1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Knock-down of Mapk8β mRNA plus Mapk9α mRNA using shRNA caused increased expression of the Prdm16 and Ucp1 genes in 3T3L1 adipocytes.
source: Similarly, knock-down of Mapk8β mRNA plus Mapk9α mRNA using shRNA caused increased expression of the Prdm16 and Ucp1 genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: NOVA-mediated alternative splicing in adipocytes contributes to adipose tissue thermogenesis.
source: Together, these data confirm that NOVA-mediated alternative splicing in adipocytes contributes to adipose tissue thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the cell autonomous effects of NOVA deficiency on thermogenic gene expression.

claim: Alternative pre-mRNA splicing expands the complexity of the transcriptome and controls isoform-specific gene expression.
source: Alternative pre-mRNA splicing expands the complexity of the transcriptome and controls isoform-specific gene expression.
evidence: General statement about alternative splicing supported by the context of the study.

claim: Obesity-induced changes in adipocyte gene expression include alternative pre-mRNA splicing.
source: We found that obesity-induced changes in adipocyte gene expression include alternative pre-mRNA splicing.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data showing differential splicing in response to HFD.

claim: Bioinformatics analysis associated part of the alternative splicing program with sequence specific NOVA splicing factors.
source: Bioinformatics analysis associated part of this alternative splicing program with sequence specific NOVA splicing factors.
evidence: Supported by bioinformatics analysis of NOVA binding sites and CLIP-seq data.

claim: Phenotypic analysis of the NOVA-deficient mice demonstrated increased adipose tissue thermogenesis and improved glycemia.
source: Phenotypic analysis of the NOVA-deficient mice demonstrated increased adipose tissue thermogenesis and improved glycemia.
evidence: Supported by metabolic and physiological measurements in NOVA-deficient mice.

claim: NOVA proteins mediate a splicing program that suppresses adipose tissue thermogenesis.
source: We show that NOVA proteins mediate a splicing program that suppresses adipose tissue thermogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the increased thermogenesis observed when NOVA proteins are absent.
